cards.title: External Validation and Simulation Purpose
cards.claim: Model validation must be specific to the intended purpose. External validation uses data not used for model building. Simulations can be based on fixed-effect estimates (typical profile), uncertainty of fixed effects (covariate effects/precision), or between-subject variability (population range). Revalidation is required if the simulation purpose differs from the original model purpose.
conditions: Applicable when preparing a model for prospective prediction or regimen optimization.
Use when distinguishing between descriptive model fit and predictive performance.
required_inputs: Provenance: Separate testing dataset for external validation; simulation settings matching the specific question.
Units/Basis: Concentration-time profiles for typical individuals or population distributions.
Prerequisites: Model must be structurally and deterministically identifiable.
Missing-input gates: If no external data is available, external validation cannot be performed; internal validation only.
limitations: Internal validation (data splitting) may reduce power to detect covariates.
Simulations based on typical estimates do not represent mean predictions unless variability is included.
Source is nonbinding guidance; specific validation strategies are project-dependent.
cards.downstream_use: Conduct external validation if data permits. Select simulation type (fixed-effect vs. variability-based) based on whether the goal is to illustrate typical behavior or population distribution.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Residuals, VPC/pcVPC, convergence, uncertainty and external prediction diagnose different issues

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
